game_events#u1.description: Whether the 2026 regular-season overtime format guarantees both teams a possession is not confirmed by the sampled rules text or by any retrieved source; the tie hazard depends heavily on it. The regulation-OT margin lattice is also not limited to 0, 3 and 6: with both teams possessing, a TD plus extra point or two-point try leaves margins of 1 and 2, which changes P(level | OT).
game_events#u1.what_would_resolve: Retrieve the 2026 NFL rulebook OT section and record the adopted format and effective season.
game_events#u1.classification_rationale: Verified: owners approved in April 2025 (effective 2025) a regular-season OT in which both teams get a possession even after an opening-drive TD, 10-minute period, ties still possible; nfl.ot_model already lists this variant. But the record's OT margin lattice of 0/3/6 is demonstrably wrong under both-possess (1, 2, 7, 8 occur), so the tie/level mechanism is wrong.
game_events#u1.catalog_action: Rewrite the game_events OT stage and nfl.ot_model measurement: fix the rule set to the 2025+ both-possess 10-minute format and replace the 0/3/6 OT margin lattice with the full lattice (1,2,3,6,7,8 incl. 2-pt tries) used for P(level | OT) and tie hazard.

season_awards#u7.catalog_action: Revise nfl.vote_outcome_model and nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty in season_awards: model ranked-ballot points (10-5-3-2-1 for MVP from 2022) with placement shares, split pre/post-2022 regimes, and record the ballot format for each other AP award.
